headline: New 'BioShock' Hack Tricks AI Browsers Into a 'Dream World' to Steal Your Data
reasoning: This topic scores highly for its exceptional clickability and viral potential, using a clever 'BioShock' inspired hack to explain a complex security flaw. While AI browsers are still an emerging category, the story has strong mainstream appeal by highlighting tangible risks like stolen passwords in a way that's easy to understand. It offers high practical value by warning users about a new class of threat and lends itself to multiple engaging formats, from explainers to hot takes.
summary: Researchers discovered a new attack, dubbed 'BioShocking,' that tricks AI browsers into a fantasy state where safety guardrails are ignored. This allows a malicious website to command the AI to perform harmful actions, like extracting user credentials or private code.

source_articles.title: New attack provides one more reason why AI browsers are a bad idea
source_articles.excerpt: Telling an LLM that 2 + 2 = 5 is enough to make it follow forbidden instructions.
